scope: backend fix-up diff (commit 75a5c8ea6) re-checked against code-review-final.json
rationale: Targeted re-check of the seven backend findings, not a fresh fan-out. Five are confirmed resolved with measurements; CR-003 is partially resolved — the semantic re-validation now exists, but the check round found five new defects inside the very code that implements it, one of them critical. The critical one matters because it is the second false-confidence defect in this run: a test named 'catastrophic regexp does not hang the worker' passed while the defense it claimed to prove did not exist, because the test used a backtracking pattern and the actual hole is in compilation. Process note, repeated from the final round: this check diff was again first built with 'git diff BASE' instead of 'BASE..HEAD', so the user's uncommitted local edit to config/customer/customer-config.yaml re-entered the review as a finding. It is not part of the branch and was dismissed a second time; the diff artifacts have been rebuilt from the branch point. All five new defects were fixed after this round (commit 7207b82ce), which also closes the emission/intake asymmetry the NEW-2 fix created: request_user_input now refuses to emit a surface with no Button carrying an action event, so the model is corrected at authoring time instead of the user being shown a form with no way to send it.

finding_notes.CR-002: Surface bounds re-applied before validation; the 3000-component surface is now refused with an error the model can act on.
finding_notes.CR-003: Semantic re-validation implemented (option membership, length caps, date bounds, regex, unknown keys, action name against Button events), but the implementation carried NEW-1..NEW-5 below.
finding_notes.CR-005: Id de-collision verified against the real validator on all three previously failing legacy shapes; converted envelopes now validate and reverse cleanly.
finding_notes.CR-006: d1c2 downgrade reconstructs the JSONB from the boolean before it is dropped, so a rollback no longer disables every assistant.
finding_notes.CR-007: Legacy fields restored on GeneratedMessage as deprecated pass-through, so continuing a legacy conversation no longer erases its interactive history.

findings.problem: The ReDoS defense bounded matching only. regex.fullmatch(pattern, value, timeout=...) cannot interrupt compilation, and nested bounded quantifiers expand the compiled program to the product of their repeat counts.
findings.impact: Measured: the 35-character pattern (((((a{20}){20}){20}){20}){20}){20} satisfies every length cap, is accepted into a surface in 0.008 s, and then costs 79.65 s in regex.compile — end-to-end intake went from 87,754 ms to 0.05 ms after the fix. A normal five-character user answer cost 0.606 s and 1.79 GB RSS one nesting level lower. The existing test asserting a catastrophic regexp cannot hang the worker passed throughout, because it used a backtracking pattern rather than a compile bomb.
findings.recommendation: Statically bound the expanded program size before compiling. A subprocess sandbox was considered and rejected: it costs tens of milliseconds per submitted field and adds a failure mode inside a threaded ASGI worker, while bounded repeats are the only construct that expands superlinearly.
findings.status: RESOLVED (budget 50k nodes; calibrated 8k -> <1 ms, 160k -> 18 ms, 64M -> 79.65 s; an adversarial sweep of 512-char patterns that pass the gate compiles in 0.35-3.63 ms)

findings.problem: action.name was matched against the surface's Button event names, but a surface declaring no Button at all left it unconstrained and unbounded.
findings.impact: 58,300 characters of attacker-chosen text reached the LLM prompt under the trusted '[Structured response to surface ...]' framing.
findings.recommendation: Cap the name independently of the surface (the surface that would license it is itself agent-authored), and reject a surface that offers no action.
findings.status: RESOLVED (cap 128 chars; the emission side now refuses to author such a surface, so the rejection cannot strand a legitimate user)

findings.problem: A nested binding path such as /user/email registered only its first segment as an allowed key, so any sibling branch under that key bypassed every per-component check.
findings.impact: A client could submit arbitrary unvalidated content under a legitimately bound top-level key.
findings.recommendation: Key bindings by full segment tuple and walk the submitted subtree down to the bound leaf, rejecting undeclared branches by full path. Bound the walk by a maximum binding depth so a 64 kB payload cannot nest tens of thousands deep.
findings.status: RESOLVED (depth cap 16; deeper bindings are ignored and therefore unanswerable rather than crashing)

findings.problem: Date bounds compared a timezone-aware submitted value against a naive min/max, which Python refuses, and the comparison was skipped.
findings.impact: Appending 'Z' to a date bypassed the declared range entirely.
findings.recommendation: Normalize both sides to UTC before comparing, reading a naive value as UTC.
findings.status: RESOLVED (a bound of a different kind than the value, e.g. a full datetime max against a time-only answer, is still skipped as a surface-authoring mismatch and is now documented in code)

findings.problem: An explicit null value skipped validation instead of being checked.
findings.impact: A null passed where the component's type contract would have rejected it.
findings.recommendation: Validate null like any other value; keep '', [] and false as the legitimate cleared-value representations.
